parameter.name: CipherList
parameter.description: Each item in this list specifies a cipher that the TLS client is allowed to use. When {{empty}} the system defaults are used.

parameter.name: CipherList
parameter.description: Each item in this list specifies a cipher that the TLS server is allowed to use. When {{empty}} the system defaults are used.

parameter.name: Certificate
parameter.description: Specifies the client certificate that must be presented to the remote server for mutual authentication. This certificate is used to authenticate the client by the remote server, ensuring that the remote server is communicating with a trusted client. The client certificate must be issued by a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) and should match the client's private key. This parameter is applicable only when a TLS session is being used.

parameter.name: CABundle
parameter.description: Specifies the group of CA certificate(s) that the client must use to validate the certificate presented by the remote server. These CA certificates form a trust chain that the server certificate must match, ensuring that only servers with trusted certificates can establish a connection. This parameter supports multiple CA certificates to accommodate different server certificate issuers. This parameter is applicable only when a TLS session is being used.

parameter.name: URL
parameter.description:
The {{datatype}} specifying the destination file location. The HTTPS transport MUST be supported, and the HTTP transport MAY be supported.
The PUT request method MUST be used to transfer the file.
This argument specifies only the destination file location, and does not indicate in any way the name or location of the local file to be uploaded.
If the Agent receives multiple upload requests with the same URL, the Agent MUST perform each upload as requested, and MUST NOT assume that the content of the file to be uploaded is the same each time.
This URL MUST NOT include the "userinfo" component, as defined in {{bibref|RFC3986}}.

parameter.name: Username
parameter.description:
Username to be used by the Agent to authenticate with the file server. If {{param}} is not provided or is set to {{empty}}, an alternative form of authentication (e.g., certificate-based authentication) is required.
Note: The mandatory requirement for this parameter was removed in Device:2.20.

parameter.name: Password
parameter.description:
Password to be used by the Agent to authenticate with the file server. If {{param}} is not provided or is set to {{empty}}, an alternative form of authentication (e.g., certificate-based authentication) is required.
Note: The mandatory requirement for this parameter was removed in Device:2.20.

The {{datatype}} specifying the source file location. The HTTPS transport MUST be supported, and the HTTP transport MAY be supported.
If the Agent receives multiple download requests with the same source URL, the Agent MUST perform each download as requested, and MUST NOT assume that the content of the file to be downloaded is the same each time.
This URL MUST NOT include the "userinfo" component, as defined in {{bibref|RFC3986}}.

Username to be used by the Agent to authenticate with the file server. If {{param}} is not provided or is set to {{empty}}, either an alternative form of authentication (e.g., certificate-based authentication) is required or no authentication is required.

Password to be used by the Agent to authenticate with the file server. If {{param}} is not provided or is set to {{empty}}, either an alternative form of authentication (e.g., certificate-based authentication) is required or no authentication is required.

parameter.name: Certificate
parameter.description: Specifies the server certificate to be presented by the server during the TLS handshake. This certificate is used to authenticate the server to remote clients, ensuring that the clients are connecting to a legitimate server. The server certificate must be issued by a trusted Certificate Authority (CA) and should match the server's private key. This parameter is applicable only when a TLS session is being used.

parameter.name: CABundle
parameter.description: Specifies the group of CA certificate(s) that the server must use to validate the certificate presented by the remote client. These CA certificates form a trust chain that the client certificate must match, ensuring that only clients with trusted certificates can establish a connection. This parameter supports multiple CA certificates to accommodate different client certificate issuers. This parameter is applicable only when a TLS session is being used.

object.name: Device.Security.Certificate.{i}.
object.description: This table provides information about all types of public key-based credentials, such as X.509 certificates, see {{bibref|RFC5280}}.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description: Enables or disables this certificate.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: User-defined name to identify and categorize the certificate (e.g., "mqtt-broker", "webserver", "vpn-client"). The implementation MAY use this name to determine which secure storage to use and how to persist the key.

parameter.name: LastModif
parameter.description: The last modification time of this certificate.

parameter.name: SerialNumber
parameter.description: The Serial Number field in an X.509 certificate, see {{bibref|RFC5280}}.

parameter.name: Issuer
NotBefore
parameter.description: The beginning of the certificate validity period; i.e. the Not Before field in an X.509 certificate, see {{bibref|RFC5280}}.

parameter.name: NotAfter
parameter.description: The end of the certificate validity period; i.e., the Not After field in an X.509 certificate, see {{bibref|RFC5280}}.

parameter.name: Subject
parameter.description: The Distinguished Name (DN) of the entity associated with the Public Key; i.e., the Subject field in an X.509 certificate, see {{bibref|RFC5280}}.

parameter.name: SubjectAlt
parameter.description:
{{list}} Each item specifies an identity that is bound to the certificate's subject, and thus bound to the Public Key.
The Subject Alternative Names extension field in an X.509 certificate, see {{bibref|RFC5280}}.

parameter.name: SignatureAlgorithm
parameter.description: The algorithm used in signing the certificate; i.e. the Signature Algorithm field in an X.509 certificate, see {{bibref|RFC5280}}.

parameter.name: RenewalMode

enumeration.description: When auto-update is triggered, the device creates a new CSR. If an existing key pair is available for this certificate, it is reused (certificate renewal as defined in {{bibref|RFC3647|Section 4.4.6}}). Otherwise, a new key pair is generated.

When auto-update is triggered, the device always generates a new key pair and creates a new CSR, regardless of whether an existing private key is available (certificate re-key as defined in {{bibref|RFC3647|Section 4.4.6}}). The existing private key is replaced once the new certificate is installed.

parameter.name: RenewalInterval
parameter.description:
Number of {{units}} before {{param|NotAfter}} at which the device automatically initiates a new CSR, as determined by {{param|RenewalMode}}. A value of 0, or {{enum|None|RenewalMode}} for {{param|RenewalMode}}, disables auto-update.
If {{param}} is greater than or equal to the certificate validity period (the interval between {{param|NotBefore}} and {{param|NotAfter}}), or if the computed trigger date ({{param|NotAfter}} minus {{param}} {{units}}) already lies in the past, the device SHOULD initiate auto-update immediately.
See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.5}} for the certificate validity period definition.

parameter.name: HasPrivateKey
parameter.description: {{true}} when the device has the private key for this certificate. {{false}} when the device does not have the private key (e.g., imported CA certificate for trust chain validation).

object.name: Device.Security.CABundle.{i}.
object.description:
This table stores information about a group of Certificate Authorities (CAs). A CA is a trusted entity that issues digital certificates used to verify the identity of servers, clients, or other entities in secure communication protocols like TLS.
This group defines a collection of trusted CA certificates that can be used to validate server certificates during TLS connections.

parameter.name: Enable
parameter.description:
Enables or disables this CA group.
When disabled, the certificates within this group will not be used for validation.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: The textual name assigned to this CA group for identification.

parameter.name: CACertificates
parameter.description: Specifies the CA certificate(s) that the client must use to validate the certificate presented by the remote server. These CA certificates form a trust chain that the server certificate must match, ensuring that only servers with trusted certificates can establish a connection. This parameter supports multiple CA certificates to accommodate different server certificate issuers. This parameter is applicable only when a TLS session is being used.

object.name: Device.Security.ClientCertificateDefault.{i}.

Default applies to KernelFault Upload command

parameter.description: {{numentries}}

object.name: Device.Security.CSR.{i}.
object.description:
This table lists the Certificate Signing Requests (CSRs) created by the device, either automatically to auto-update an existing certificate or in response to a {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}}. When a certificate is installed whose public key matches that of a CSR, the CSR is automatically deleted.
If no certificate is installed before the timeout defined by {{param|.Security.CSRTimeout}} expires, the CSR entry is automatically deleted. Its associated private key is also deleted, unless it is already referenced by an existing {{object|#.Certificate}} entry (e.g., in {{enum|Renew|RenewalMode}} mode).
If a pending entry with the same {{param|Name}} already exists when {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} is invoked, the device SHOULD reject the new operation with a 7005 (Resources Exceeded) fault code. The Controller MAY cancel the pending request via {{command|.LocalAgent.Request.{i}.Cancel()}}, which causes the device to remove the CSR entry and its associated private key (unless referenced by an existing {{object|#.Certificate}} entry), before retrying.

parameter.name: EncodedCSR
parameter.description: The CSR in PEM format (PKCS#10, signed by the device, Base64 encoded with header and footer).

parameter.name: DateCreated
parameter.description: Date and time the CSR was created.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: User-defined name to identify the certificate, as specified in the {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} command that generated this CSR. This name is associated with the certificate when it is added via {{command|.Security.AddCertificate()}}.

parameter.name: BasicConstraints
parameter.description:
The Basic Constraints extension specified when creating the CSR, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.9}}.
When {{true}}, the certificate is a CA certificate (CA:TRUE).
When {{false}}, the certificate is an end-entity certificate (CA:FALSE).

parameter.name: PathLengthConstraint
parameter.description:
The path length constraint specified when creating the CSR, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.9}}.
Specifies the maximum number of non-self-issued intermediate certificates that may follow this certificate in a valid certification path. A value of zero means this certificate may be directly followed only by end-entity certificates. Where no path length constraint was specified, no upper limit is imposed.
This parameter is meaningful only when {{param|BasicConstraints}} is {{true}} and {{enum|KeyCertSign|KeyUsageList}} is present in {{param|KeyUsageList}}.
The value -1 indicates that no path length constraint was specified in the CSR, or that {{param|BasicConstraints}} is {{false}}.

parameter.name: KeyUsageList
parameter.description: Each item specifies a Key Usage purpose specified when creating the CSR, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.3}}.

parameter.name: ExtendedKeyUsageList
parameter.description: Each item specifies an Extended Key Usage (EKU) purpose for the certificate, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.12}}. The EKU extension indicates the purposes for which the certificate public key may be used.

parameter.name: RenewalMode
parameter.description: The automatic certificate update mode requested when this CSR was created.

enumeration.description: When auto-update is triggered, the device creates a new CSR. If an existing key pair is available for this certificate, it is reused (certificate renewal as defined in {{bibref|RFC3647|Section 4.4.6}}). Otherwise, a new key pair is generated.

When auto-update is triggered, the device always generates a new key pair and creates a new CSR, regardless of whether an existing private key is available (certificate re-key as defined in {{bibref|RFC3647|Section 4.4.6}}). The existing private key is replaced once the new certificate is installed.

parameter.name: RenewalInterval
parameter.description:
Number of {{units}} before the NotAfter date at which the device automatically initiates a new CSR, as determined by {{param|RenewalMode}}. A value of 0, or {{enum|None|RenewalMode}} for {{param|RenewalMode}}, disables auto-update.
If {{param}} is greater than or equal to the certificate validity period (see {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.5}}), or if the computed trigger date already lies in the past, the device SHOULD initiate auto-update immediately.

parameter.name: CommandKey
parameter.description: The ''command_key'' supplied in the {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} Operate message that generated this CSR. This value can be used to correlate this CSR entry with the resulting {{event|#.CSRCreated!}} or {{event|#.CSRFailure!}} event, and eventually the certificate added via {{command|.Security.AddCertificate()}}. This will be {{empty}} if the CSR was automatically created due to certificate auto-update rather than an explicit controller request.
When auto-update is triggered, a {{event|#.CSRCreated!}} event is generated upon successful creation of the new CSR, or a {{event|#.CSRFailure!}} event if the attempt fails.

command.name: GetCertificateURI()
command.description: Returns the path to the X.509 certificate and its corresponding private key that is associated with the entry of the {{object}} table.

parameter.name: CertificateURI
parameter.description: The absolute or relative path to the certificate file, specified as an {{bibref|RFC8089}} (The file URI Scheme).

parameter.name: PrivateKeyURI
parameter.description:
The URI for the private key associated with this certificate, formatted according to {{bibref|RFC7512}}. This URI should point to the key's location on a hardware security module (HSM) or other cryptographic token.
For security reasons, the URI MUST NOT include any PIN information (e.g.,`pin-value`). The service responsible for managing the token should inject the required PIN at runtime. This practice prevents unauthorized access and malicious reuse of the private key by other services.

command.name: CADir()
command.description:
Returns the path to the directory containing CA certificates.
This is necessary for services, especially microservices in host or container environments requiring mTLS, to locate the appropriate CA certificates during configuration.
Depending on the security requirements a service-specific CA directory may be required.

parameter.name: CADir
parameter.description: This parameter specifies the absolute or relative path to the directory containing the CA certificate bundle, specified as an {{bibref|RFC8089}} URI (The file URI Scheme).

command.name: CAFile()
command.description:
Returns the path to a file containing one or more CA certificates.
This is necessary for services, especially microservices in host or container environments requiring mTLS, to locate the appropriate CA certificates during configuration.
Depending on the security requirements a service-specific CA file may be required.

parameter.name: CAFile
parameter.description: The absolute or relative path to the file containing the CA certificate(s), specified as an {{bibref|RFC8089}} URI (The file URI Scheme).

command.name: Update()
command.description:
Updates the CA bundle with new certificate content. The new bundle completely replaces the existing CA certificates.
For example, if the current bundle contains 5 CA certificates and the new bundle contains only 3 CA certificates, the 2 CA certificates that are not present in the new bundle will be deleted.
If the update fails, the previous bundle is kept as-is.
The device SHOULD reject the operation with the following fault codes for specific error conditions:
* If the bundle does not contain valid PEM formatted certificates, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7265 (Invalid PEM Format) fault code.
* If the bundle could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7262 (Failed To Import Bundle) fault code.
* If one or more certificates in the bundle could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7263 (Failed To Import Certificate) fault code.
* If there is insufficient disk space to store the CA bundle, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7266 (Insufficient Disk Space) fault code.

parameter.name: Bundle
parameter.description: One or more X.509 CA certificates in PEM format, concatenated into a single PEM file.

parameter.name: NumberOfCertificates
parameter.description: The number of CA certificates successfully installed from the bundle.

object.description: This table provides a default Certificate and CABundle for commands such as {{command|Device.DeviceInfo.FirmwareImage.{i}.Download()}} when called without an explicit Certificate or CABundle as a parameter.

parameter.description: Specifies the command this entry applies to.

parameter.name: SupportedBundleFormats
parameter.description: Each item indicates a bundle format that is supported by the {{command|AddCertificateBundle()}} command.

command.name: AddCertificateBundle()
command.description:
The device installs the new bundle and updates the `Device.Security.Certificate.{i}`. The bundle (e.g., PKCS#12, PEM) contains both a certificate and a private key.
If a certificate with the same {{param|Device.Security.Certificate.{i}.SerialNumber}} and {{param|Device.Security.Certificate.{i}.Issuer}} already exists in the device, the existing certificate is replaced with the new certificate, and the {{param|Certificate}} output parameter references the updated entry.
The device SHOULD reject the operation with the following fault codes for specific error conditions:
* If the specified bundle format is not supported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7260 (Bundle Format Not Supported) fault code.
* If the bundle signature verification fails, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7261 (Bundle Signature Failure) fault code.
* If the bundle could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7262 (Failed To Import Bundle) fault code.
* If the certificate in the bundle could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7263 (Failed To Import Certificate) fault code.
* If the private key in the bundle could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7264 (Failed To Import Private Key) fault code.
* If the certificate has a SerialNumber and Issuer that match an existing certificate with a different Name, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7270 (Certificate Identity Conflict) fault code.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description:
An optional input the Controller can use to specify the {{param|.Security.Certificate.{i}.Alias}} value for the added entry.
If provided as an input and the value already exists in {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}}}, this command will fail.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description:
User-defined name to identify the certificate.
If a certificate with the same Name already exists in {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}.}}, the existing certificate will be replaced with the certificate from the bundle.

parameter.name: BundleFormat
parameter.description: The format of the bundle.

parameter.name: Bundle
parameter.description:
The bundle containing the certificate and private key. It is good practice for the bundle to be encrypted and signed.
How the bundle is decrypted, verified, and installed on the system depends on the device design and is considered implementation specific.

parameter.name: Certificate
parameter.description: Specifies the location where the certificate was installed.

command.name: AddCABundle()
command.description:
The device installs the new CA bundle and adds an entry to the {{object|Device.Security.CABundle.{i}.}} table.
If a CA bundle with the same {{param|Device.Security.CABundle.{i}.Name}} already exists in the device, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7267 (Duplicate CA Bundle Name) fault code.
The device SHOULD reject the operation with the following fault codes for specific error conditions:
* If the bundle does not contain valid PEM formatted certificates, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7265 (Invalid PEM Format) fault code.
* If the bundle could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7262 (Failed To Import Bundle) fault code.
* If one or more certificates in the bundle could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7263 (Failed To Import Certificate) fault code.
* If there is insufficient disk space to store the CA bundle, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7266 (Insufficient Disk Space) fault code.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description:
An optional input the Controller can use to specify the {{param|.Security.CABundle.{i}.Alias}} value for the added entry.
If provided as an input and the value already exists in {{object|.Security.CABundle.{i}}}, this command will fail.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: The name of the new CA bundle.

parameter.name: Bundle
parameter.description: One or more X.509 CA certificates in PEM format, concatenated into a single PEM file.

parameter.name: CABundle
parameter.description: Specifies the location where the CA bundle was installed.

parameter.name: NumberOfCertificates
parameter.description: The number of CA certificates successfully installed from the bundle.

parameter.name: CSRTimeout
parameter.description:
The number of {{units}} a pending {{object|.Security.CSR.{i}.}} entry is retained before being automatically deleted. Its associated private key is also deleted, unless it is already referenced by an existing {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}.}} entry (e.g., in {{enum|Renew|.Security.CSR.{i}.RenewalMode}} mode).
A CSR entry is considered pending until a matching certificate is installed via {{command|.Security.AddCertificate()}}. This timeout applies to all CSR entries, regardless of whether they were created explicitly via {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} or automatically during an auto-update cycle.
A value of 0 disables automatic expiry.

command.name: CreateCSR()
command.description:
This command causes the device to generate a CSR using a locally-created and secure private key. {{param|RenewalMode}} determines whether an existing key pair is reused ({{enum|Renew|RenewalMode}}) or a new one is always generated ({{enum|ReKey|RenewalMode}}), both for the current invocation and for future auto-update cycles.
{{param|RenewalInterval}} controls when the auto-update is triggered relative to the certificate expiry date.
If a pending {{object|.Security.CSR.{i}.}} entry with the same {{param|Name}} already exists, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7005 (Resources Exceeded) fault code. The Controller MAY cancel the pending request via {{command|.LocalAgent.Request.{i}.Cancel()}}, which causes the device to remove the CSR entry and its associated private key (unless referenced by an existing {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}.}} entry), before retrying.
If a {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}.}} entry with the same {{param|Name}} already exists, it remains in place until the new certificate is installed via {{command|AddCertificate()}}.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: User-defined name to identify and categorize the certificate (e.g., "mqtt-broker", "webserver", "vpn-client"). The implementation MAY use this name to determine which secure storage to use and how to persist the key.

parameter.name: KeyType
parameter.description: Identifier for the type of asymmetric key pair the device is to create for the CSR. Common examples include RSA (see {{bibref|RFC8017}}), ECDSA with P-256, ECDSA with P-384, Ed25519, and Ed448.

parameter.name: KeyLength
parameter.description: The length of the key to be created, in {{units}}. Only applicable when {{param|KeyType}} specifies RSA; for RSA, common values are 2048 and 4096 {{units}}. For other key types (e.g., ECDSA, Ed25519, Ed448), the key length is fixed by the algorithm and this parameter is ignored.

parameter.name: BasicConstraints
parameter.description:
The Basic Constraints extension specified when creating the CSR, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.9}}.
When {{true}}, the certificate is a CA certificate (CA:TRUE).
When {{false}}, the certificate is an end-entity certificate (CA:FALSE).

parameter.name: PathLengthConstraint
parameter.description:
The path length constraint to request in the CSR, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.9}}.
Only applicable when {{param|BasicConstraints}} is {{true}}. Specifies the maximum number of non-self-issued intermediate certificates that may follow this certificate in a valid certification path. A value of zero means this certificate may be directly followed only by end-entity certificates.
The value -1 indicates that no path length constraint is requested.

parameter.name: KeyUsageList
parameter.description: Each item specifies a Key Usage purpose for the certificate, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.3}}. The Key Usage extension defines the cryptographic operations for which the certificate public key may be used. This parameter is optional in the CSR, and the CA may apply its own policy when issuing the certificate.

enumeration.description: Digital signature (verify signatures on data other than certificates and CRLs).
Certificate signing (sign certificates). Typically used for CA certificates.
CRL signing (sign certificate revocation lists). Typically used for CA certificates.

parameter.name: ExtendedKeyUsageList
parameter.description: Each item specifies an Extended Key Usage (EKU) purpose for the certificate, as defined in {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.12}}. The EKU extension indicates the purposes for which the certificate public key may be used. This parameter is optional in the CSR, and the CA may apply its own policy when issuing the certificate.

parameter.name: SubjectAlternativeName
parameter.description: Subject Alternative Name entries to include in the CSR. The SAN extension allows additional identities to be bound to the certificate subject, such as DNS names, IP addresses, URIs, or email addresses. Modern certificates often rely primarily on SAN rather than the CN field. At least one of {{param}} or {{param|CommonName}} must be specified to identify the certificate subject. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.2.1.6}} for the Subject Alternative Name extension.

parameter.name: CommonName
parameter.description: Common Name to include in the CSR. This maps to the CN attribute in the Subject field of the certificate's Distinguished Name. The CN typically identifies the entity to which the certificate is issued, such as a hostname or service name. At least one of {{param}} or {{param|SubjectAlternativeName}} must be specified to identify the certificate subject. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.4}} for DN attribute type definitions and {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.6}} for usage in the Subject field.

parameter.name: OrganizationName
parameter.description: Organization Name to include in the CSR. This maps to the O attribute in the Subject field of the certificate's Distinguished Name. The O attribute identifies the organization to which the certificate subject belongs. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.4}} for DN attribute type definitions and {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.6}} for usage in the Subject field.

parameter.name: OrganizationalUnit
parameter.description: Organizational Unit to include in the CSR. This maps to the OU attribute in the Subject field of the certificate's Distinguished Name. The OU attribute identifies a subdivision or department within the organization. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.4}} for DN attribute type definitions and {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.6}} for usage in the Subject field.

parameter.name: Locality
parameter.description: Locality to include in the CSR. This maps to the L attribute in the Subject field of the certificate's Distinguished Name. The L attribute identifies the city, town, or village where the organization is located. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.4}} for DN attribute type definitions and {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.6}} for usage in the Subject field.

parameter.name: State
parameter.description: State or province name to include in the CSR. This maps to the ST attribute in the Subject field of the certificate's Distinguished Name. The ST attribute identifies the state or province where the organization is located. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.4}} for DN attribute type definitions and {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.6}} for usage in the Subject field.

parameter.name: Country
parameter.description: Country name to include in the CSR. This maps to the C attribute in the Subject field of the certificate's Distinguished Name. The C attribute is a two-letter country code as defined in {{bibref|ISO3166-1}}. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.4}} for DN attribute type definitions and {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.6}} for usage in the Subject field.

parameter.name: Email
parameter.description: Email address to include in the CSR. This maps to the Email attribute in the Subject field of the certificate's Distinguished Name. The EMAIL attribute provides a contact email address for the certificate subject. See {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.4}} for DN attribute type definitions and {{bibref|RFC5280|Section 4.1.2.6}} for usage in the Subject field.

parameter.name: RenewalMode
parameter.description: The automatic certificate update mode to apply once the certificate is installed.

enumeration.description: When auto-update is triggered, the device creates a new CSR. If an existing key pair is available for this certificate, it is reused (certificate renewal as defined in {{bibref|RFC3647|Section 4.4.6}}). Otherwise, a new key pair is generated.

When auto-update is triggered, the device always generates a new key pair and creates a new CSR, regardless of whether an existing private key is available (certificate re-key as defined in {{bibref|RFC3647|Section 4.4.6}}). The existing private key is replaced once the new certificate is installed.

parameter.name: RenewalInterval
parameter.description:
Number of {{units}} before the certificate expires at which the device automatically initiates a new CSR, as determined by {{param|RenewalMode}}. A value of 0 disables auto-update.
If {{param}} is greater than or equal to the certificate validity period, or if the computed trigger date already lies in the past, the device SHOULD initiate auto-update immediately.

parameter.name: EncodedCSR
parameter.description: The CSR in PEM format (PKCS#10, signed by the device, Base64 encoded with header and footer). Returned upon successful completion of the command.

command.name: AddCertificate()
command.description:
This command is issued to add a new certificate to {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}.}}. The certificate, provided in PEM format, is parsed to populate the parameters of the Certificate table. If {{param|MatchToCSR}} is {{true}}, the private key that was used to sign the matching CSR is associated with the certificate and the CSR is deleted.
If a certificate with the same {{param|Name}} already exists, the existing certificate entry is replaced with the new certificate. This replacement involves: * The old certificate and its associated private key are securely deleted * The new certificate is added with the new private key (from the matching CSR) * The {{param|Name}} is assigned to the new certificate entry
The device SHOULD reject the operation with the following fault codes for specific error conditions:
* If {{param|MatchToCSR}} is {{true}} and no matching CSR was found for the certificate, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7268 (No Matching CSR) fault code.
* If the certificate could not be imported, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7263 (Failed To Import Certificate) fault code.
* If the certificate has a SerialNumber and Issuer that match an existing certificate with a different Name, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7270 (Certificate Identity Conflict) fault code.

parameter.name: Alias
parameter.description:
An optional input the Controller can use to specify the {{param|.Security.Certificate.{i}.Alias}} value for the added entry.
If provided as an input and the value already exists in {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}.}}, this command will fail.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description:
User-defined name to identify the certificate.
When {{param|MatchToCSR}} is {{true}}, the name from the matching CSR is used instead.
When {{param|MatchToCSR}} is {{false}}, this parameter MUST be specified.
If a certificate with the same name already exists, it will be replaced.

parameter.name: Certificate
parameter.description: The X.509 certificate in PEM {{bibref|RFC7468}} format.

parameter.name: MatchToCSR
parameter.description: {{true}} if the certificate being added is in response to a CSR sent by the device, otherwise {{false}}. If {{true}}, info from the matching CSR, including private key and name, is associated with the certificate and the CSR deleted. If {{true}} and no matching CSR is found, the device SHOULD reject the operation with a 7268 (No Matching CSR) fault code.

parameter.name: RenewalMode
parameter.description: The automatic certificate update mode to apply to the resulting {{object|.Security.Certificate.{i}.}} entry.

parameter.name: RenewalInterval
parameter.description: Number of {{units}} before the certificate expires at which the device automatically initiates a new CSR, as determined by {{param|RenewalMode}}. A value of 0 disables auto-update.

event.name: CSRCreated!
event.description: This event notifies a USP Controller that the device has created a new CSR.

parameter.name: CommandKey
parameter.description: The ''command_key'' supplied in the {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} Operate message that generated this CSR. This value correlates the event with the original command invocation and the CSR entry in {{object|.Security.CSR.{i}.}}. This will be {{empty}} if the CSR was automatically created due to certificate auto-update.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: User-defined name to identify the certificate, as specified in the {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} command that generated this CSR. This name is associated with the certificate when it is added via {{command|.Security.AddCertificate()}}.

parameter.name: EncodedCSR
parameter.description: The CSR in PEM format (PKCS#10, signed by the device, Base64 encoded with header and footer).

event.name: CSRFailure!
event.description: This event notifies a USP Controller that the device has tried but failed to create a new CSR.

parameter.name: CommandKey
parameter.description: The ''command_key'' supplied in the {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} Operate message that failed. This value correlates the event with the original command invocation. This will be {{empty}} if the failure occurred during an automatic certificate auto-update attempt.

parameter.name: Name
parameter.description: User-defined name to identify the certificate, as specified in the {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} command that generated this CSR. This name is associated with the certificate when it is added via {{command|.Security.AddCertificate()}}.

parameter.name: FaultCode
parameter.description: A non-zero USP fault code indicating the reason the CSR creation failed. If the failure occurred during an auto-update cycle and no {{command|.Security.CreateCSR()}} Operate message was involved, this reflects the internal error condition.

parameter.name: FaultString
parameter.description: A human-readable description of the fault. SHOULD be {{empty}} if {{param|FaultCode}} is 0.
